data.cultural_impact: The name Shivaniya has deep roots in Hindu culture and history. Lord Shiva is revered as the God of destruction and renunciation, and is one of the primary deities in Hinduism. Shivaniya carries the blessings and divine influence of this powerful and revered deity, adding a profound cultural significance to the name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lord Shiva is seen as the embodiment of purity, detachment, and renunciation. By carrying the name Shivaniya, one is infused with the spiritual essence of these qualities, invoking the divine presence of Lord Shiva in one's life. The name adds a spiritual depth and significance to the individual's identity, serving as a daily reminder of the divine force that resides within.

historical_references.reference: Shivaniya is an ancient Hindu name derived from the God Shiva. The name is believed to have originated in the Mahabharata era, around 400 BCE. It is mentioned in the Mahabharata that Arjuna, one of the Pandava brothers, had a charioteer named Shivani.
historical_references.context: Ancient Hindu text, Mahabharata, mentions the name Shivaniya for Arjuna's charioteer.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name Shivaniya can be found in the Puranic literature of Hinduism, specifically in the Skanda Purana. In this text, Shivaniya is described as a manifestation of Goddess Parvati, consort of Lord Shiva. She is said to have appeared before the sage Markandeya and granted him a boon, thereby earning the name Shivaniya.
historical_references.context: Puranic text, Skanda Purana, describes Shivaniya as a manifestation of Goddess Parvati.
